newsitem.title: CANADA: Pratt & Whitney to get Canadian aid.
newsitem.headline: Pratt & Whitney to get Canadian aid.

text.p: The Canadian government said on Thursday it would be providing financial assistance to United Technologies Corp's Pratt & Whitney Canada.

The federal department Industry Canada said Industry Minister John Manley would announce two investments in the company under the government's Technology Partnerships Canada program on Friday, when the amount was to be disclosed.
The program provides government money for research and development for specific projects, which are to be repaid as the products go to market.

Critics have called these "investments" interest-free loans to profitable companies, but Manley's spokesman Bill Milliken said the deals were structured so the government could make money if sales went well.

Western Canadian politicians have also criticized the predominance of technology investments in Quebec. The head of Pratt & Whitney was outspoken against Quebec separation from Canada during a 1995 referendum campaign, but Milliken said such projects were decided strictly on their merit.
Two-thirds of the Pratt & Whitney investments will be used in Quebec and the other third in Halifax, Nova Scotia.
